subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: Should empty-scope plugin reloads preserve only maintainer-approved always-on harnesses, restore all previously registered harnesses, or intentionally clear every harness until the next activation?
rationale: The source problem is real, but the safe fix depends on the plugin lifecycle and security contract for plugin-owned harnesses after an empty or disabled scope.

options.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
options.body: Filter restoration to the agreed always-on/native harness contract and prove disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses are cleared.

options.title: Accept restore-all semantics
options.body: Allow all prior harnesses to survive empty-scope reloads, but document and test that plugin disablement no longer clears those harnesses in this path.

options.title: Clear all on empty scope
options.body: Keep empty-scope reloads fail-closed and solve user-facing failures through earlier readiness, config validation, or dispatch retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter restoration to the agreed always-on/native harness contract and prove disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses are cleared.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the harness registry and appears closest to the cross-cutting plugin/runtime ownership boundary.
